public_rationale: Altman supported regulation in his Senate testimony. During the same month's European tour, he met regulators and objected to classifications that would impose additional safety obligations. Contemporary reporting also reproduced OpenAI's disclosure of EU lobbying contacts. This supports the ordinary reading of overlapping public support and efforts to reduce particular requirements. It does not establish insincerity or same-day lobbying.
limitations: The temporal reading is material: a requirement for an EU weakening request on the exact hearing date would remain unresolved.
Supporting regulation generally is compatible with opposing particular provisions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: While Altman publicly supported AI regulation in 2023, OpenAI lobbied to water down the EU AI Act.

statement.excerpt: And even as Altman was telling Congress that he supported AI regulation, his company was lobbying the EU to water down its AI act.
statement.document_title: Two Years Ago Today in AI History: The Tale of An About-face in AI Regulation

from_speaker: even as Altman was telling Congress
his company was lobbying the EU
to water down its AI act
our_interpretation: Read 'even as' as the same May 2023 regulatory episode surrounding the congressional testimony, rather than requiring lobbying on the exact hearing date.
Watering down means seeking to reduce proposed legal obligations or exclude OpenAI's models from stricter requirements. It does not require opposition to every regulation.
The claim concerns public positions and lobbying, not whether Altman sincerely believed his testimony.
criteria.support_condition: Records show Altman publicly supporting regulation in Congress and OpenAI advocating reduced EU AI Act obligations during the same May 2023 episode.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records establish that Altman did not support regulation in that testimony, or that the attributed EU advocacy did not seek reduced obligations.
